steps.title: Clear the board
steps.say: Let's wipe the crowded graph and use a simple everyday example instead.

steps.title: One price, few buyers
steps.say: Imagine ice cream costs $2 and 10 people want to buy it today.

steps.title: A hot day arrives
steps.say: Now it gets hot. At the very same $2, more people want ice cream, so 30 people show up.

steps.title: That is a shift
steps.say: Wanting more at the same price is what we call a demand shift. The price did not cause it; the weather did.

ops.text:
More wanted at the same price
= demand shifts right

steps.title: Not enough ice cream
steps.say: But the seller only made 10 scoops. With 30 buyers and 10 scoops, people compete for them.

steps.title: Price rises
steps.say: The seller notices the line and raises the price to $3. Some buyers drop out, and the market settles. That is why higher demand pushes price up.
